title: Implement risk scoring v0 thresholds + docs + unit tests (batching/caching suggestions)
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Context
We’re shipping a beta “Optimization suggestions” experience in Console. Each suggestion (batching/caching) must include a simple risk label (Low/Medium/High) with an explanation that’s consistent and conservative.

This ticket implements the v0 risk scoring thresholds, documents the rationale/inputs, and adds unit tests using representative workloads to avoid regressions.

References
- Confluence ADR: adr-risk-scoring-model-v0 (inputs/approach + iteration plan)
- Confluence copy guidance: risk-level-definition-and-copy-guidelines (UI language expectations)
- Guardrails doc: suggestions-guardrails-and-constraints (constraints that should influence risk)
- Slack thread: eng-ml/1771722205-risk-scoring-inputs-and-confidence (conservative defaults + confidence bands)

Scope
1) Implement v0 thresholds in the scoring module used by the suggestions compute job (not in the Console).
2) Produce a short internal doc section that explains:
   - what “risk” means (performance/reliability risk; not security)
   - which inputs are used
   - how we map to Low/Medium/High
   - how we treat missing/low-confidence telemetry
   - how we should iterate safely (backwards compatible; avoid label churn)
3) Add unit tests for threshold boundaries and representative workload scenarios.

Non-goals
- No new UI copy changes (Design owns; we just document what we emit and why).
- No ML model training; v0 is deterministic thresholding and conservative heuristics.
- No customer-specific overrides beyond existing guardrails.

Implementation plan
A) Risk inputs (already available / expected)
We should score based on the same aggregated telemetry window used for savings estimates:
- request rate (QPS) per route/model
- latency distribution: baseline p50/p95 and variability (e.g., p95/p50 ratio)
- concurrency / queueing pressure signals (if available in aggregates)
- sequence length distribution (p50/p95 input+output tokens)
- cache hit rate (for caching suggestions) and hit-rate confidence / sample count
- batching headroom signals (batch size distribution, current batch wait time if available)
- error rate / recent 5xx spikes (should make us more conservative)

B) Proposed v0 label mapping (deterministic)
We emit BOTH:
- risk_level: LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH
- risk_reasons: list of machine-readable reason codes (to drive consistent UI explanations)
- confidence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW (separate from risk; used to explain uncertainty)

Core logic (high level)
- Start at LOW.
- Promote to MEDIUM/HIGH based on the max of triggered conditions.
- If confidence is LOW due to insufficient samples or staleness, bump at least to MEDIUM unless the suggestion is “very safe” (see below).

Threshold guidance (initial)
These values are chosen to be conservative; exact numbers can be tuned, but tests should pin behavior at boundaries.

1) Latency sensitivity / tight SLO routes
- If baseline p95 latency is already near known SLO (if SLO exists in config), treat as HIGH for batching suggestions that increase queueing risk.
- If no explicit SLO: use heuristic
  - if baseline p95 < 250ms AND route is tagged “interactive” (from route metadata), batching risk >= MEDIUM
  - if baseline p95 < 150ms AND interactive, batching risk = HIGH
Reason codes:
- BASELINE_LATENCY_LOW_INTERACTIVE
- SLO_HEADROOM_LOW

2) Variability / tail risk
- If (p95 / p50) >= 3.0, risk >= MEDIUM
- If (p95 / p50) >= 5.0, risk = HIGH
Reason codes:
- TAIL_LATENCY_VOLATILE

3) Load / queueing pressure
- If concurrency high and current queueing (or inferred queueing) is non-trivial, batching risk >= MEDIUM
- If sustained near-capacity (e.g., high utilization signal from aggregates), batching risk = HIGH
Reason codes:
- HIGH_CONCURRENCY
- CAPACITY_PRESSURE

4) Cache recommendations safety
Caching changes tend to be safer than batching, but can cause memory pressure / eviction churn.
- If cache hit-rate confidence is LOW (few samples) => risk >= MEDIUM
- If suggested cache footprint increase is above a conservative threshold (from estimator) => risk = HIGH
Reason codes:
- INSUFFICIENT_CACHE_SAMPLES
- CACHE_FOOTPRINT_INCREASE_HIGH

5) Error-rate guardrail
- If baseline 5xx rate > 0.5% over the scoring window => risk >= MEDIUM
- If > 1.0% => risk = HIGH
Reason codes:
- ERROR_RATE_ELEVATED

6) Staleness / missing telemetry
- If telemetry window is missing critical inputs OR stale beyond compute staleness budget => risk >= MEDIUM + confidence LOW
Reason codes:
- TELEMETRY_INCOMPLETE
- TELEMETRY_STALE

"Very safe" exception
If suggestion is caching-only AND (cache sample count high) AND baseline route not interactive AND no error-rate elevation, allow LOW even if some minor inputs missing (but keep confidence MEDIUM).

C) Documentation
Add a section to the internal risk scoring ADR page (or a sibling doc if ADR is immutable) describing:
- risk vs confidence
- reason codes and what they mean
- how we change thresholds going forward (versioning + minimizing label churn)
- recommended monitoring: distribution of risk levels over time + churn rate

D) Unit tests
Add tests that cover:
1) Boundary tests for each threshold (e.g., p95/p50 exactly 3.0 and 5.0)
2) Representative workload scenarios (table-driven tests)
   - “Interactive chat route, low baseline p95, high concurrency” => HIGH for batching
   - “Batch processing route, high p95, stable tails” => LOW/MEDIUM depending on other signals
   - “Caching suggestion with low cache samples” => MEDIUM + confidence LOW
   - “Elevated 5xx despite good latency” => MEDIUM/HIGH (should not be LOW)
   - “Stale telemetry” => MEDIUM + confidence LOW
3) Regression tests for reason codes: ensure expected reasons are emitted for each scenario.

Representative workloads (seed values)
We should hardcode a small set of fixtures (sanitized) to mirror common customer patterns:
- SaaS support chat (interactive): small prompts, tight latency
- Reranking endpoint: low latency requirement, high QPS bursts
- Document processing (async): long outputs, tolerant latency
- Finance/report generation: moderate QPS, long context, stability matters

Acceptance criteria
- Risk scoring module returns (risk_level, confidence, reason_codes) deterministically for given aggregate inputs.
- Unit tests cover thresholds + at least 5 scenario fixtures; all pass.
- Documentation updated with rationale and a clear definition of risk vs confidence.
- Scoring behavior is conservative: missing/low-confidence telemetry never yields LOW unless it’s caching-only and explicitly safe.

Rollout notes
- This will affect user trust; any threshold changes after beta start should be gated and monitored for label churn.
- Coordinate with Console team so UI tooltips match reason codes emitted.

Open questions
- Do we have route metadata for “interactive” tagging today, or do we infer from route type? (If missing, default to conservative MEDIUM for batching on unknown.)
- Where do we source explicit per-route SLOs, if present? If not available, rely on heuristics only.

Owner checklist
- [ ] Implement thresholds + reason codes
- [ ] Add fixtures + tests
- [ ] Update doc section + link in suggestions service overview
- [ ] Post summary in #eng-ml and #eng-platform threads with the chosen thresholds

Links
- Linear: ENG-19436
- Related: ENG-19419 (estimator inputs), ENG-19455 (compute scheduling + staleness)
- GitHub PRs: (to be linked)
comments: 2026-01-24 — Sana Farid: Drafted initial thresholds proposal based on eng-ml thread. Biggest question is interactive detection (route metadata vs heuristic). Leaning toward conservative MEDIUM/HIGH for batching when unknown.
2026-01-29 — Hassan Mirza: +1 on separate confidence from risk. For caching, footprint/memory pressure is the real risk; avoid marking caching LOW if estimator predicts large KV/prefix cache growth.

2026-02-03 — Logan Wright: Telemetry aggregates provide p50/p95 latency, request count, error-rate, token length percentiles. Concurrency is partial (we have in-flight gauge only for hosted; dedicated/private may be missing). Please handle missing concurrency as unknown => do not downgrade risk.

2026-02-06 — Dylan Brooks: Please ensure reason codes are stable and documented. Console is building tooltips off these. We also need tests that pin reason-code ordering/deduping so UI doesn’t flicker.
2026-02-10 — Chloe Martin: Add staleness handling: if aggregates older than compute SLA, force confidence LOW and risk >= MEDIUM. This aligns with stale_as_of being exposed to UI.
2026-02-14 — Sana Farid: Implemented scoring + reason codes in feature branch. Added 6 scenario fixtures. Pending: doc update + review from Applied ML and Console.
2026-02-18 — Jonas Weber: Reviewed fixtures; suggest adding one where tail ratio is high even at moderate p95 to ensure volatility triggers MEDIUM/HIGH. Also ensure boundary at p95/p50=5.0 is HIGH.

2026-02-21 — Sana Farid: Addressed Jonas feedback; added tail-volatility fixture + boundary tests. Doc section drafted; requesting final review from Marissa/Tessa for terminology alignment (risk != security).
